title: Better Not Drive Home

patient.name: Mr Anand Krishnan
patient.presenting_complaint: About to be dilated, but plans to drive to a meeting straight after

history.hpc: Mr Anand says 'After this I drive to my meeting, can right?' He is charted for dilation of both eyes for a fundus check and intends to drive immediately after, which needs to be addressed.
history.pmhx: No narrow-angle history. No drug allergies (confirm).

investigations.task: Dilate both eyes and clearly educate the patient that he should not drive until the dilation wears off
investigations.key_points: Dilation blurs near vision and causes light sensitivity for about 4–6 hours; advise not to drive afterwards and to arrange alternative transport; offer to dilate after addressing his plans

diagnosis: Both eyes are dilated and the patient is clearly counselled that dilation blurs vision and causes light sensitivity for several hours, so he should not drive until it wears off. The OA addresses his plan to drive, advises alternative transport, and documents the dilation. This is a procedural/education station.

immediate: Confirm identity, the eyes to dilate and the order
Check for drug allergy and absence of a narrow-angle contraindication
Explain that dilation will blur vision and cause light sensitivity for about 4–6 hours
Advise clearly that he should not drive until it wears off and suggest alternative transport
Record pre-dilation pupil sizes, instil the charted drops (no-touch), note dosage and time
Document the dilation and the advice given
follow_up: Confirm the patient has a safe way home / onward
Inform the doctor of the dilation time for the fundus exam
patient_education: Explain dilation blurs near vision and increases light sensitivity for a few hours
Advise not to drive until vision returns to normal
Suggest sunglasses and arranging a lift or public transport

key_points: Confirms identity, eyes to dilate and the order
Checks for drug allergy and narrow-angle contraindication
Asks about the patient's plans after the appointment
Instils the charted dilating drops with a no-touch technique
Offers measures for light sensitivity (e.g. sunglasses)
Knows dilation causes blur and light sensitivity for ~4–6 hours
Recognises driving after dilation is unsafe
Clearly advises not to drive and suggests alternative transport
Documents the dilation and the advice given
